findings.text: follow-on: the committed run directory's record set is enumerated in two places with no shared owner. _review_input_identities globs committed/run/<run_id>/*.json to key each record (_directory_identity on the run dir plus _file_identity per file), while review.stored_record inlines the same enumeration (sorted(run_directory.glob("*.json"))) to pick the record it returns. The two must agree on what the committed tree holds for the key to describe the read that was actually made; plan reviews already have the shared enumerator (_candidate_paths in plan_review.py, which reads committed plan/<slug>/ first). A private committed-run-record-paths helper in review.py, used by both, would spell the rule once. Modest, because both sites currently glob the identical shape, but it is a second copy of a filename rule the store already owns.

justifications.durability: The added cases name concrete regressions: committing a record must move the memo key (test_a_committed_review_write_changes_the_memo_key), an unchanged tree must leave the key in force so the memo is not defeated (test_an_unchanged_committed_tree_leaves_the_key_in_force), and a composed review over an uncommitted plan must leave a blob git cat-file -e resolves. The declared control reddens the first case. I falsified both halves independently in a scratch tree of the reviewed head: leaving the committed tree out of the key reddens test_a_committed_review_write_changes_the_memo_key (1 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1, review-negative-control.log), and dropping -w reddens the composition case (1 failed, 2 passed, EXIT=1, review-negative-control-blob.log). Neither failing id appears in the head arm's 3 passed.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced: head extraction 3 passed EXIT=0; both mutations red with the expected ids and EXIT=1. The recorded gate (112 passed) and the reviewed run's own control (1 failed) are consistent with the reviewed logs.
justifications.fit: The change extends the owners the plan names: committed_review_root and COMMITTED_RUN_DIRNAME from reckon/crew/review.py are reused rather than a second path rule, and the -w flag is added to the existing git hash-object call rather than a new store path.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Both halves of the dispatch goal are present and load-bearing: the committed run directory and its records join the classification key, a committed record settles the run as having its own (no store-wide staging search), and the plan-review composition writes the reviewed bytes with -w.
justifications.reuse: Reuses review_module.committed_review_root, _directory_identity, _file_identity and contextlib.suppress; adds no new mechanism. One duplication remains: the committed run directory's *.json enumeration is now inlined here as well as in review.stored_record (see the follow-on).
justifications.scope_discipline: Three files changed, all declared; no figure was written where the orientation file list named a figures directory, and no path outside the declaration is touched.
